paper_metadata.title: Cyclic oxidation behavior of Fe-Cr modified slurry silicide coated Nb-18.7Si alloyed with Ti and Zr

evidence.quote: The near eutectic Nb-Si based alloys possessing Nbss (Nb-Si solid solution)/Nb3Si-Nb5Si3 microstructure are potential high-temperature materials for high-altitude and hypersonic applications.

other.slurry_composition: Si, Fe and Cr mixed in ratio 60:20:20 (wt.%)

evidence.quote: elemental powders of high purity Si, Fe and Cr were mixed in the ratio of 60:20:20 (wt.%) in a suitable liquid medium to form a slurry, which was subsequently applied on the sample surfaces by brushing.

The samples were diffusion heat treated in vacuum at 1400°C for 2h to effect interdiffusion between the Fe, Cr, Si contained in the slurry and Nb from the substrate, which was essential for the formation of the diffusion silicide coating .

evidence.quote: elemental powders of high purity Si, Fe and Cr were mixed in the ratio of 60:20:20 (wt.%) in a suitable liquid medium to form a slurry, which was subsequently applied on the sample surfaces by brushing.

The samples were diffusion heat treated in vacuum at 1400°C for 2h to effect interdiffusion between the Fe, Cr, Si contained in the slurry and Nb from the substrate, which was essential for the formation of the diffusion silicide coating .

evidence.quote: The outer layer of the coating contained 33 at.% Nb, 67 at.% Si and minor amounts of Fe and Cr (1-2 at.%). The atom ratio of 1:2 for Nb:Si indicated that the outer layer contained the NbSi2 phase

For the Nb-18.7Si and the Nb-18.7Si-5Ti alloys, the bright and gray phases corresponded to the Nb solid solution (Nbss) and Nb3Si, respectively, and their relative phase percentages were about 28.7 and 68.5%.

For the Nb-18.7Si and the Nb-18.7Si-5Ti alloys, the bright and gray phases corresponded to the Nb solid solution (Nbss) and Nb3Si, respectively, and their relative phase percentages were about 28.7 and 68.5%.
Some minor amount of the α-Nb5Si3 phase (2.8%) was also present in both the above alloys
The substrate in the coated Nb-18.7Si-5Zr alloy contained 56% of Nbss and 44% of α-Nb5Si3 phases and no Nb3Si phase was detected

the outer bright oxide scale was rich in Nb-oxide and exhibited elongated plate like morphology
the inner nodular dark phase regions were rich in silica and had a relatively smooth appearance
the bright scale exhibited more of a disk-shaped morphology (Fig. 9b), which was unlike its plate-like elongated morphology observed at the lower oxidation temperature of 800°C
The dark phase was nodular (Fig. 9a) and primarily constituted of silica (Fig. 9e).
A careful examination of the oxide scale also indicated the formation of an innermost continuous thin layer of Cr-oxide (region 3 in Fig. 14).

Several through-thickness cracks were observed in the coating cross-section (Fig. 1), which occurred due to the thermal stresses generated during cooling of the coating-substrate ensemble from the diffusion heat treatment temperature.

a closer examination revealed the localized formation of a layer of silicate scale having dendritic morphology at the interparticle boundaries (Fig. 9c). The dendritic structure was indicative of the formation of eutectic liquid during oxidation at 1400°C.

The resistance against oxidation was achieved by the formation of a protective oxide scale on the surface

The parabolic oxidation kinetics suggested that the superficial oxide scale served as an effective barrier against the inward diffusion of oxygen from the ambient to the oxide-scale/coating interface, which thereby lowered the oxidation rate substantially

The onset of weight loss in the coated samples, observed after ~300 min. of oxidation (Fig. 7b), occured due to the cracking and spallation of the oxide scale under the influence of thermal stresses arising during the repititive heating and cooling oxidation test cycles
The dendritic structure was indicative of the formation of eutectic liquid during oxidation at 1400 °C. The Nb2O5-SiO2 phase diagram suggests the formation of eutectic liquid at 1448°C
The absence of the Nb3Si phase can be ascribed to the presence of Zr, which promoted the eutectoid transformation of the Nb3Si phase into Nbss and α-Nb5Si3
